function: DRL agent decides when to refresh the RIS tile exclusion (deactivating shadowed tiles), balancing channel-gain enhancement against update cost; tile choice is a closed-form threshold (p. 3, 5-9).
system: Indoor 5x5x3 m rooms, four ceiling mmWave APs, 1-8 mobile users, 1,500+ near-passive reflecting RIS tiles per wall, 28 GHz; antenna numbers not stated (p. 1, 3-4).
method: Actor-critic reinforcement learning, PPO-like with clipped objective and entropy; Gaussian stochastic policy, fused drift-timer state, shaped reward; 2,304 parameters; trained on a single wall (p. 7-9, 11).
data_channel: Custom indoor 28 GHz simulator: AP-RIS-UE gains, LoS blockage by shadow-area method, semi-Markov Levy-walk mobility generator [17], [19]; 100 training and 100 validation trajectories per layout (p. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Train on one wall of one layout; validate on 100 new trajectories across 12 wall-layout pairs and in a 10x10 m room R4 (agent from R2) (p. 8-10, 14).
baselines: Non-learned: fixed update timing found by exhaustive search; NSGA-II discussed only. Learned: DQN, DDPG, TD3, TRPO, SAC and PPO variants, compared on return (p. 13-14).
metrics: Channel-gain enhancement eta net of update cost, eta per decision update, capacity loss (bit/s/Hz), cumulative return, number of updates (p. 5-6, 12-14).
complexity: 2,304 learnable parameters; actor cost O(8 N_fusion + 2 N_fusion^2), 4,608 FLOPs; under 5 ns on FPGA/Jetson, at least 15 us on Raspberry Pi (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 1: "Given the absence of a general mmWave channel model"; the gains come from the authors' own indoor simulator with shadow-area blockage [19] (p. 5), only the mobility parameters use real-world measurements (p. 10), and no 3GPP or other standard channel is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "deploying an agent trained in R2 directly in a room four times larger, R4"; p. 8: the actor trains on a single wall and is validated across different walls and layouts.
q3_support: p. 13: "the results of the non-learning method, i.e., the fixed timing method, applied through an exhaustive search"; p. 14: "We compared various state-of-the-art DRL training frameworks, including PPO, TRPO, SAC, deep Q-network (DQN)", scored on return in Fig. 9(c).
q4_support: p. 12: "requiring a floating-point computational requirement of no less than 4, 608 FLOPs"; p. 11 gives the actor cost O(8 N_fusion + 2 N_fusion^2) and 2,304 parameters.
q5_support: p. 10: "There are 100 UE mobility trajectories used for training in each layout", produced by the authors' generator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 3 (RIS configuration): the learned part is the timing of RIS tile-exclusion updates, while tile selection is the closed-form threshold of Theorem 1 (p. 5-6). The reviewer should confirm that update timing counts as RIS configuration and not as above-PHY control management. q3: Fig. 9(c) on p. 12 scores PPO, DQN, SAC, TRPO, TD3 and DDPG variants by the ratio of runs reaching the highest return; the learned baselines are standard DRL algorithms run on the paper's own state and reward design, so the reviewer may regard them as variants of the proposed agent. Tile phase control is assumed well designed (p. 4). The speeds on p. 12 are estimates for FPGA, Jetson and Raspberry Pi, not measurements.
